title: Russian Attacks Kill 3, Injure 38 Nationwide as Drones Torch Zaporizhzhia Shopping Mall
detail: Russian forces attacked Ukraine nationwide over September 6-7, killing at least 3 people and wounding 38 others, a day after US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner's inconclusive first visit to Kyiv for renewed peace talks. Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 92 attack drones overnight, of which 71 were shot down or intercepted. In Kherson, Russian artillery shelled the Dniprovskyi district around 10:30 a.m., killing a 65-year-old woman in her apartment; drone strikes injured 8 more residents of Kherson and Darivka, and a separate strike in Novovorontsovka wounded another civilian, bringing the oblast's toll to 2 killed and 14 wounded. In Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, 1 person was killed and 6 wounded. Zaporizhzhia was hit by an overnight drone barrage that set a 700-square-meter shopping mall ablaze in six separate fires, injuring 2 people at a nearby parking area though officials reported no casualties at the mall itself; 40 rescuers and 10 units of equipment responded. Kharkiv Oblast reported 5 wounded (men aged 25, 47, 50, 52 and 69), Donetsk Oblast 7 wounded, Sumy Oblast 2 wounded from mortar and artillery shelling, and Odesa Oblast a drone hit on a house with no reported injuries.

media.caption: Fire at a Zaporizhzhia shopping center after an overnight Russian drone attack, September 7, 2026

title: Trump Set to Call Putin, Then Zelensky, as Kyiv Peace Push Ends Without Breakthrough
detail: A day after US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner wrapped their first visit to Kyiv — meeting President Volodymyr Zelensky twice with UK, French, and German national security advisers joining a third session — a US official told the Kyiv Independent that President Trump would consult with the envoys before calling Vladimir Putin and then Zelensky, with both calls expected on September 7. The official said the sequencing reflected the White House's view that a lasting settlement requires Russia's direct participation. The Kyiv round of talks produced no diplomatic breakthrough: Zelensky told reporters 'we expect the war will continue,' saying Ukraine is instead counting on US energy and air defense support for the coming winter. Kushner said the US still hoped to restart trilateral US-Russia-Ukraine negotiations. The reciprocal 72-hour pause on long-range strikes against Moscow and Kyiv, agreed to accommodate the shuttle diplomacy, had expired.

media.caption: US officials say Trump plans to call Putin, then Zelensky, after the inconclusive Kyiv peace push, September 7, 2026
